NVIDIA Isaac GR00T N1.7 (3B vision-language-action policy) running on one Tenstorrent Blackhole p150a via tt-nn, in the DROID layout: two cameras × two frames (t−15 and t) at 16:9, a 17-dim Franka state and a task instruction in, a 40-step chunk of end-effector, gripper and joint actions out. Stage-2 release: the whole DiT denoise runs as one persistent megakernel streaming bfp8 weights from a DRAM arena; vision (tuned Qwen3-VL tower), LLM and adapter are TTNN ops in Metal traces; `GR00T_DIT_BACKEND=ttnn` selects the Stage-1 denoise.

RLWRLD RLDX-1 PT-IMG (vision-language-action policy: Qwen3-VL-8B backbone truncated to 18 layers with 64 cognition tokens, FLUX-style MM-DiT "MSAT" action head, 4 Euler steps) running on one Tenstorrent Blackhole p150a via tt-nn, in the DROID layout: three cameras × one frame at 320×180, a 7-dim end-effector / gripper state and a task instruction in, a 16-step chunk of DROID end-effector deltas and gripper targets out. The ViT and the LLM are TTNN ops in Metal traces; the MSAT denoise runs as one persistent megakernel streaming bfp8 weights from a DRAM arena. tt-metal's fast-dispatch kernels run on the chip's idle Ethernet cores, which frees the full 12×10 worker grid for the model.

BEVDet-R50-4DLongterm-Depth, a 76M-parameter camera-only 3D detector with temporal fusion: a ResNet-50 + FPN image encoder with a camera-aware depth network (118 depth bins) on six cameras at 256x704, a BEVPool v2 lift-splat into a 128 x 128 bird's-eye-view grid (±51.2 m), fusion of the last 8 BEV maps, a ResNet + FPN BEV encoder and a CenterPoint-style head (498 GFLOPs per frame). Six surround-view camera images go in, with their intrinsics and camera-to-`base_link` extrinsics (and optionally the ego pose for motion-compensated fusion). Out come 3D boxes with scores and velocities for the 10 nuScenes classes and the Autoware label of each, with the pre- and post-processing of the `autoware_tensorrt_bevdet` node (resize and crop, BEV history, box decoding, Scale-NMS, label mapping). The image and BEV encoders run on the device; the lift-splat between them, the image resize and the NMS run on the host.

BEVFormer-small, a 59.5M-parameter camera-only 3D detector (ResNet-101 with deformable convolutions in stages 3 and 4 and a one-level FPN, a 3-layer spatiotemporal BEV encoder over a 150x150 bird's-eye view that attends to the previous frame's BEV and to the six cameras, a 6-layer DETR decoder with 900 queries), run on six 1280x736 network inputs (about 1.97 TFLOPs per frame) through the graph of the TensorRT export Autoware deploys. Six surround-view camera images with their calibration and the ego pose go in. Out come 3D boxes with scores and velocities for the 10 nuScenes classes and the Autoware label of each, with the pre- and post-processing of the `autoware_tensorrt_bevformer` node (resize to 1600x900, normalisation, camera geometry, top-300 decode, label mapping). Each stream keeps its previous BEV on the device as temporal history.

BEVFusion-L, the lidar-only model of the weights repo (`bevfusion_lidar.onnx`, 8.3M parameters): hard voxelization (0.17 x 0.17 x 0.2 m voxels on a 1440 x 1440 x 41 grid) with a mean voxel encoder, a 21-layer sparse 3D convolution encoder to a 180 x 180 bird's-eye-view map, a SECOND backbone with a SECONDFPN neck and a TransFusion head (heatmap, top-500 object queries, one transformer decoder layer). It uses the LiDAR only: no camera input. One point cloud in `base_link` goes in (x, y, z; one sweep, or Autoware's two-sweep densified cloud with a `time_lag` column; intensity is not used). Out come Autoware `DetectedObjects`-equivalent 3D boxes for CAR, TRUCK, BUS, TRAILER, BICYCLE and PEDESTRIAN, with the pre- and post-processing of the `autoware_bevfusion` node (voxelization, two-sweep densification, score threshold, yaw-norm gate, circle and IoU NMS, area-based class remapper).

CenterPoint, the LiDAR 3D object detector Autoware runs by default, and its CenterPoint-tiny variant: a PointPillars pillar encoder (PFN 9-16-32), a SECOND backbone, a SECONDFPN neck and a single-task CenterPoint head, on a 480x480 head grid (base) or a 240x240 one with a stride-2 first block (tiny, a quarter of base's compute). One LiDAR point cloud in `base_link` goes in (one sweep, or Autoware's 2-sweep densified cloud). Out come 3D boxes of CAR, TRUCK, BUS, TRAILER, BICYCLE and PEDESTRIAN equivalent to Autoware's `DetectedObjects`, with the pre- and post-processing of the `autoware_lidar_centerpoint` node (voxelization, decode, circle NMS, IoU NMS, area-based class remap).

Depth Anything 3, metric branch (DA3Metric-Large: DINOv2-L backbone + DPT head, 0.35 B params) for metric monocular depth in metres, with the 24-block backbone running on one Tenstorrent Blackhole p150a via tt-nn: image in, 518×518 depth map in metres out.
Weights: [depth-anything/DA3Metric-Large](https://huggingface.co/depth-anything/DA3Metric-Large) · Paper: [arXiv:2511.10647](https://arxiv.org/abs/2511.10647) · Upstream code: [ByteDance-Seed/Depth-Anything-3](https://github.com/ByteDance-Seed/Depth-Anything-3) · Port: [changh95/tt-Depth-Anything-3](https://github.com/changh95/tt-Depth-Anything-3)

Diffusion Planner v5.0, a 14.55M-parameter diffusion-transformer planner: six MLP-Mixer entity encoders and a 6-block transformer fusion encoder over 564 scene tokens, a 3-block DiT decoder with adaLN (self-attention over the ego and 320 agents, cross-attention to the scene) evaluated 11 times by a 10-step DPM-Solver++(2M) loop, and a turn-indicator head; the whole plan runs on the device. The 15 planner tensors of the Autoware node go in (ego and neighbour histories, lanes with speed limits, route lanes, polygons, line strings, goal pose, ego shape, turn-indicator history, in the ego frame). Out come an 8 s ego trajectory (80 poses at 10 Hz with velocity and acceleration), an 8 s predicted path for every valid neighbour and a turn-indicator command, with the pre- and post-processing of the `autoware_diffusion_planner` node (input normalization, agent ordering, velocity smoothing, force stop, turn-indicator decision).

FRNet, a 10.0M-parameter LiDAR semantic-segmentation network (a frustum feature encoder of point-wise MLPs with a per-cell max, a frustum-range 2D CNN with four residual stages and point-pixel fusion, and a per-point head), one network per sensor: the Hesai OT128 on a 128x1024 frustum grid (about 1.25 TFLOPs per sweep at 80,000 points) and the Hesai QT128 on 128x256 (about 0.36 TFLOPs at 60,000 points), selected by serve profile. One LiDAR sweep in the sensor frame (x, y, z, raw 0-255 intensity) goes in. Out come a class id and its probability for every point (27 T4 classes) and the node's filtered-cloud mask, with the pre- and post-processing of the `autoware_lidar_frnet` node (ego crop box, frustum projection, Autoware's point interpolation, argmax, class filter).

HaMeR (Hand Mesh Recovery, ViT-H/16 + MANO regression head) running on one Tenstorrent Blackhole p150a via tt-nn: a full frame plus one hand box in, MANO pose/shape/camera out (and, with your own MANO_RIGHT.pkl, the 778-vertex mesh and 21 joints).

DUSt3R two-view 3D reconstruction (naver/DUSt3R_ViTLarge_BaseDecoder_512_dpt: ViT-L/16 encoder, dual-branch decoder, two DPT heads; the backbone of MASt3R) running entirely on one Tenstorrent Blackhole p150a via tt-nn: an image pair in, two dense 512×512 pointmaps with confidence (plus optional PairViewer pose) out.

METEOR v157, a 48.25M-parameter camera-only perception and planning network (a ResNet-34 + FPN image encoder over the eight cameras, 2D segmentation, depth, 2D detection and traffic-light heads, a depth-gated lift to one 800x500 bird's-eye view at 0.2 m, BEV heads for lanes, 3D detection, occupancy, agent futures and risk, and an ego planner), run on eight 768x432 camera images (2.58 TFLOPs per frame). Eight raw, unrectified surround-view images with their intrinsics and extrinsics and the ego speed go in. Out come 3D boxes (vehicle / VRU) with stationary flags and futures, per-camera 2D boxes, the ego-relevant traffic light, a BEV lane map and three ego paths with steer, acceleration and brake, with the pre- and post-processing of METEOR's C++ runtime (resize, calibration-dependent lift tables, thresholds, NMS, plan-mode hysteresis, temporal smoothing per stream).

This package runs the [Pi-0.5](https://huggingface.co/lerobot/pi05_base) VLA model of Physical Intelligence on one Tenstorrent Blackhole p150a.

- Supports the following configurations:
  - num_cameras: 1/2/3/4
  - Prompt bucket: 32/64/128/224
  - Action chunk: 1~64 (in 32/64 bucket)
  - 1 to 16 flow-matching steps (N).
  - batch: 1
  - Total 32 presets are available.
- Built on megakernel principle using `ttnn.generic_op` - not in a sense that the entire model is a single operation, but rather, main operations are fused into a single operation.
  - VISION: SigLIP and the projector (one device program for each group of 2 cameras)
  - PREFIX: the Language embedding and the Gemma-2B prefill, which writes the KV caches
  - EXPERT: the action expert (N steps x 18 layers) with its adaRMS time conditioning, the action input and output projections and the Euler steps.
- The default configuration with 2 cameras, action chunk of 50 actions and 10 steps, with 142 token-long prompt, the inference time is 55.2 ms (non-scalable profile) and 56.5 ms (scalable profile).

Weights: [lerobot/pi05_base](https://huggingface.co/lerobot/pi05_base) ·
Paper: [arXiv:2504.16054](https://arxiv.org/abs/2504.16054) ·
Upstream code: [Physical-Intelligence/openpi](https://github.com/Physical-Intelligence/openpi) ·
Port: [changh95/tt-pi-0.5](https://github.com/changh95/tt-pi-0.5)

- This package runs on **p150** (mesh `P150`, one p150a), with two serve profiles:
  - `non-scalable` (default): Ethernet cores do the dispatch, so the vision and prefix programs get a 12 x 10 worker grid. The chip cannot join a multi-chip fabric in this mode.
  - `scalable`: Tensix cores do the dispatch (11 x 10 worker grid). The Ethernet cores stay free for a multi-chip fabric.
- The package uses [tt-model-manager](https://github.com/tenstorrent/tt-model-manager) 0.1.0 (manifest schema 5.1).

PointPainting, a camera-LiDAR 3D object detector: the 2-D detections (ROIs) of up to 8 rectified cameras are projected onto the LiDAR points as 3 additive class bits, then a PointPillars pillar encoder (PFN 12-16-32), a SECOND backbone, a SECONDFPN neck and a single-task CenterPoint head on a 760x480 grid detect the objects. One LiDAR point cloud in `base_link` goes in, with the cameras' calibration and their 2-D detections (one sweep, client-side past sweeps or server-side 2-sweep densification). Out come 3D boxes of CAR, TRUCK, BUS, TRAILER, BICYCLE and PEDESTRIAN equivalent to Autoware's `DetectedObjects`, with the pre- and post-processing of the `pointpainting_fusion` node (painting, densification, voxelization, decode, circle NMS, IoU NMS, area-based class remap). The 2-D detector itself is not included.

Point Transformer V3, a 34.0M-parameter LiDAR network: 0.12 m voxels serialized along two Morton curves, a 5-stage encoder (sparse-conv positional encoding, attention over patches of 512 voxels, grid pooling; about 0.36 TFLOPs on a 117,000-voxel frame), a segmentation decoder for 15 classes and a TransFusion-style BEV detection head (top-500 queries). One concatenated LiDAR cloud in `base_link` (x, y, z, intensity 0-255) goes in. Out come, per input point, a class, its probability, the normalised entropy, Autoware's `PointCloudClassification` value and the obstacle-cloud membership, and with the `seg_det` profile 3D boxes for 7 classes (CAR, TRUCK, BUS, BICYCLE, PEDESTRIAN, TRAFFIC_CONE, BARRIER), with the pre- and post-processing of the `autoware_ptv3` node (crop, voxelization, serialization, source reconstruction, score threshold, NMS, class remapping).

Qwen-Image-2.1 (Alibaba Qwen's 7B single-stream DiT text-to-image / editing model, with its Qwen3-VL-8B
text encoder and 64-channel RGBA VAE) running on one Tenstorrent Blackhole p150a via tt-nn: prompt in,
1024x1024 PNG out, all three sub-models on the chip, the 40-step denoise as one metal trace.
Weights: [Qwen/Qwen-Image-2.1](https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen-Image-2.1) · Port: `code/models/experimental/qwen_image_2_1` in this repo

Meta's SAM3 (Segment Anything with Concepts, 840.5M params) for text-prompted open-vocabulary instance segmentation, with the ViT-H/14 backbone and fusion encoder running on one Tenstorrent Blackhole p150a via tt-nn: image plus noun phrases in, per-instance masks, boxes and scores out.
Weights: [facebook/sam3](https://huggingface.co/facebook/sam3) · Paper: [arXiv:2511.16719](https://arxiv.org/abs/2511.16719) · Upstream code: [facebookresearch/sam3](https://github.com/facebookresearch/sam3) · Port: [changh95/tt-sam3](https://github.com/changh95/tt-sam3)

SceneSeg, a 48.3M-parameter camera segmentation network (EfficientNet-B0 encoder, a SceneContext block that gates the stride-32 features with a global prior, and a UNet-style decoder of five 2x up-blocks with a 3-class head) on a fixed 640x320 input (367 GFLOPs per frame). One camera image of any size goes in. Out come the VisionPilot foreground mask (mono8, 255 = foreground, at the input's size) and a 3-class map (background, foreground objects, drivable road), with the pre- and post-processing of the `scene_seg_model` node (squash to 640x320 with OpenCV's INTER_LINEAR, ImageNet normalisation, argmax, nearest-neighbour resize back).

StreamPETR, an 82M-parameter camera-only 3D detector with a temporal object memory: a VoVNet-99-eSE + CPFPN image backbone on five cameras at 480x640, the PETR 3D position embedding (computed once per calibration) and a 6-layer transformer decoder over 644 learned and 256 propagated queries with a 1,024-row object memory kept on the device (about 1,100 GFLOPs per frame). Five surround-view camera images go in, with their intrinsics, camera-to-`base_link` extrinsics, the frame's time stamp and ego pose. Out come 3D boxes with scores and velocities for CAR, TRUCK, BUS, BICYCLE and PEDESTRIAN, with the pre- and post-processing of the `autoware_camera_streampetr` node (resize, crop and normalization, memory ego-motion compensation and resets, decoding from all six decoder layers, per-class score thresholds, IoU-BEV NMS).

TransFusion-L (`t4xx1_90m`), the LiDAR-only TransFusion detector of Autoware's opt-in `lidar_transfusion` node: a PointPillars pillar encoder (11 decorated features, PFN 32-64) on a 768x768 pillar grid, a SECOND backbone, a SECONDFPN neck and a TransFusion head (dense heatmap, 3x3 local maximum, top-500 object queries, one transformer decoder layer over the 192x192 BEV, box heads). One LiDAR point cloud in `base_link` goes in (x, y, z and 0-255 intensity; one sweep, or Autoware's 2-sweep densified cloud). Out come 3D boxes of CAR, TRUCK, BUS, TRAILER, BICYCLE and PEDESTRIAN equivalent to Autoware's `DetectedObjects`, with the pre- and post-processing of the `autoware_lidar_transfusion` node (voxelization, decoration, decode, circle NMS, IoU NMS, area-based class remap).

X-VLA-base (the cross-embodiment vision-language-action model, lerobot checkpoint: Florence-2 encoder + soft-prompted flow-matching transformer) running on one Tenstorrent Blackhole p150a via tt-nn: 3 camera views + an instruction + proprio state in, a 30-step x 20-D action chunk out.
Weights: [lerobot/xvla-base](https://huggingface.co/lerobot/xvla-base) · Paper: [arXiv:2510.10274](https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.10274) · Upstream code: [2toinf/X-VLA](https://github.com/2toinf/X-VLA) · Port: [changh95/tt-XVLA](https://github.com/changh95/tt-XVLA)

YOLOX-s+ seg16, a 15.5M-parameter single-stage camera detector (ELAN CSPDarknet backbone, PAFPN neck, anchor-free decoupled head on strides 8, 16 and 32) with a 16-class semantic-segmentation decoder, run on a 960x960 letterboxed input (121 GFLOPs per image). One camera image of any size goes in. Out come 2D boxes for 8 classes (UNKNOWN, CAR, TRUCK, BUS, BICYCLE, MOTORBIKE, PEDESTRIAN, ANIMAL), the Autoware ROI records and a 16-class semantic mask, with the pre- and post-processing of the `autoware_tensorrt_yolox` node (letterbox, decode, NMS, class remap, ROI overlay on the mask).
